brief: Fixed income is winning global investor flows in 2026: YTD inflows equal 7.9% of AUM versus 1.3% for equities, spanning high grade, munis and loans. US flows are led by government bonds, and global bond-fund flows run above the historical median for this point in September. Investors still favor protection, with short-duration and inflation-protected funds seeing sustained inflows, the latter accelerating over the past year, while retail flows now support bond ETFs too. Asset managers' net-long Treasury futures positioning sits near cycle highs, TLT just posted its largest inflow since September 2024, and long-dated Treasury ETF flows outpaced investment-grade credit in August, pointing to demand for duration specifically. But the bond market has not returned the love: the recent selloff has been unusually broad and global, driven by term premia, rate expectations, inflation compensation and real rates, pushing long-end yields back toward pre-GFC levels. Goldman estimates roughly $5tn of issuance this year and $5.2tn next, and BofA flags AI-investment credit demand as a possible canary for rates. Despite that, bond volatility remains muted even as positioning grows crowded. The note's own close states flows are bullish, positioning is crowded, supply is enormous, and something has to give.
